interpretations: Count rentals per rating by joining rental to inventory to film, then take the mean of the per-rating counts as the overall average. Keep ratings with a count strictly above it, and return the mean of their counts and the mean of (count − overall average)
Same as above, but keep ratings with a count greater than or equal to the overall average
Count distinct rental_id values per rating rather than joined rows, so that any duplicate rows from the joins are not counted twice
Treat "rental transactions" as payment records: link payment to rental to inventory to film, count payments per rating, and apply the same above-average filter and the two averages
Treat "rental transactions" as only the rentals that have a payment, excluding rentals with no payment
Treat "rental transactions" as only completed rentals with a non-null return_date
Define the overall average as total rentals divided by the number of ratings, including any ratings with zero rentals, rather than the average over ratings that appear in the join
Define the overall average count as the average number of rentals per film within each rating, then compare per-film rental averages across ratings
Return the second value as the average of (count − overall average) over the above-average ratings, which equals the first value minus the overall average
Return the second value as the average excess as a percentage or ratio of the overall average, rather than an absolute number of rentals
Return the two values as two columns in one row, with the first being the average count and the second the average excess
Compute the overall average over all ratings including the above-average ones, versus excluding the above-average ones, i.e. compare against the mean of the remaining ratings

queries:
WITH counts AS (
  SELECT f.rating AS rating, COUNT(*) AS cnt
  FROM rental r
  JOIN inventory i ON r.inventory_id = i.inventory_id
  JOIN film f ON i.film_id = f.film_id
  GROUP BY f.rating
),
overall AS (
  SELECT AVG(cnt) AS avg_cnt FROM counts
)
SELECT AVG(c.cnt) AS avg_count, AVG(c.cnt - o.avg_cnt) AS avg_diff
FROM counts c
CROSS JOIN overall o
WHERE c.cnt > o.avg_cnt;
SELECT rating, COUNT(*) AS film_count
FROM film
GROUP BY rating
HAVING COUNT(*) >= (SELECT AVG(cnt) FROM (SELECT COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM film GROUP BY rating))
SELECT f.rating, COUNT(DISTINCT r.rental_id)
FROM rental r
JOIN inventory i ON r.inventory_id = i.inventory_id
JOIN film f ON i.film_id = f.film_id
GROUP BY f.rating
WITH rating_stats AS (
  SELECT f.rating,
         COUNT(p.payment_id) AS payment_count,
         AVG(f.rental_rate) AS avg_rental_rate,
         AVG(f.length) AS avg_length
  FROM payment p
  JOIN rental r ON p.rental_id = r.rental_id
  JOIN inventory i ON r.inventory_id = i.inventory_id
  JOIN film f ON i.film_id = f.film_id
  GROUP BY f.rating
)
SELECT rating, payment_count, avg_rental_rate, avg_length
FROM rating_stats
WHERE payment_count > (SELECT AVG(payment_count) FROM rating_stats);
SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT r.rental_id) FROM rental r JOIN payment p ON p.rental_id = r.rental_id;
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM rental WHERE return_date IS NOT NULL;
